way_names.W5: the Rift: Drover's bridge, the mouth ferry, the desert line viaduct

the ridge col.why: the Frostline's lip: the valley's way up to the tarn (W2)

the Fells saddle.why: the High Fells path over the shoulder east of the tarn

the Lode notch.why: the mule track's top, at the mine mouth

the Rime glacier.why: above the tarn: the ice caves are under its snout (act 1, the Rime Wyrm)

the West ice.why: the massif's western ice field, past the walk

erg.note: the dune sea: tall transverse dunes

desert.note: the sand sheet and interdune flats: low ripples

edges.forest: a darker rim on every forest edge (trees and ground)
edges.moor: the Brackens' heath a touch more heather-coloured, with a thin darker edge against the valley
edges.ash: the fire country's ash: a dark rim and a fall-off of ash flecks onto the ground beside it
edges.fens: the moss fens drawn with a marsh pattern (water lines and tufts)
edges.floodplain: the Lull's watermeadows cooler, with a dotted flood line at their edge
edges.sand to steppe: the dune sea, sand sheet, scrub and steppe blended over about 100 px (no hard edge)

usable_land.definition: land cells outside the frame that are walkable or built on (8 px cells)

Crossroads.purpose: the market and meeting point of the valley: four lanes and two roads meet here; the farms round it bring grain, wool and fruit to its market, and the halt, the mill and the smithy serve the whole valley
Crossroads.setting: the valley floor either side of the Sleepwater, on its flat terraces; the woodland and the stone circle to the north-west
neighbourhoods: the zone as built: the square, the well, the bakery, the herbalist, the smithy, the library
south along the Sleepwater: the mill, the granary, millers' and carters' cottages
south-west down the lane to the halt: cottages with long gardens, the halt and its goods shed
east where the Foothill Road and the Lull Road leave: the drovers' market, the inn, the farrier
a short row on the woodland's skirt, foresters' and hurdle-makers' cottages

outskirts.name: the halt farms
outskirts.why: grain, hay and apples for the market

outskirts.name: the mill farms
outskirts.why: wheat for the mill, orchards on the river terrace

Dust Gulch.purpose: the desert line's railhead and the Lode's ore yard: ore comes down the mule track to the depot, goods and water go out along the line; repair shops, the assay office and the corrals for the caravans; the Amber gives it water
Dust Gulch.setting: where the Amber leaves the mountains, on the gravel fan either side of the river; desert all round, the Glass field to the west
neighbourhoods: the frontier main street: the saloon, the store, the sheriff (Pendle), the assay office
the platform, the goods yard and sheds, the repair shop and the water tower
homes along the river and its gardens, behind the main street
homes and the chapel on the west bank
pens and stables for the caravans and the mule trains, east of town

outskirts.name: the corrals
outskirts.why: pens and stables for the caravans and the mule trains

outskirts.name: the goods yard
outskirts.why: the desert line's sidings and the ore bins

outskirts.name: the ore yard
outskirts.why: the Lode's ore, down the mule track, waiting for the train

outskirts.name: the river gardens
outskirts.why: irrigated from the Amber: vegetables, figs, fodder

Palm Spring.purpose: the first water in the dry country: the Willow Run comes up again in the spring; irrigated gardens, date and fig orchards, the caravans' rest on the Drover's Road, and the diviner (Mirra) who keeps the spring
Palm Spring.setting: round the spring pool and along its two channels, on the gravel where the Willow Run resurfaces; scrub and steppe round it
neighbourhoods: houses round the pool under the palms
the inn, stables and stores on the Drover's Road
gardeners' houses along the south-west channel
along the south-east channel to the orchards

outskirts.name: the date gardens
outskirts.why: date palms, figs and vegetables on the channels

outskirts.name: the north grove
outskirts.why: palms along the Willow Run

Fernhollow.purpose: timber from the Fern hills' wet woods: the sawmill, the wood yards and the joiners; charcoal for Cogsworth; its own green, school and chapel, on the Foothill Road halfway between Crossroads and Cogsworth
Fernhollow.setting: a clearing in the woods of the Fern hills, where the Foothill Road crosses Fern Lane
neighbourhoods: houses round the village green, the chapel and the school
the sawmill and the wood yards, joiners and coopers
cottages down the lane to the Lull Road

outskirts.name: the wood yards
outskirts.why: the Fern hills' timber, seasoning in stacks

Cogsworth.purpose: coal and iron from the coal hills, the fast Cog for power (the Millrace), and the railway out: the foundry, the mills, the engine works and the terminus; brick terraces for the workers between the works and the pits
Cogsworth.setting: the Cog's east bank where the valley opens, between the river and the coal hills; the pits and spoil heaps above it
neighbourhoods: the foundry, the mills on the Millrace, workshops by the river
shops and the works offices on the towpath road down to the terminus
brick workers' terraces climbing toward the pits
the platform, the station square and the Garth Road's start

outskirts.name: the railway yard
outskirts.why: the terminus sidings, the engine shed and the coal stage

Hearthold.purpose: the fire country's town of knights and crafts: the castle on its rock commands the only stable ground between the lava flows; armourers, smiths, potters and vintners under the walls; the lower town on the flat ground below, toward the springs and the coast
Hearthold.setting: a rock between two lava flows below the crater, the walls round its top; the old flow's weathered ground below it farmed
neighbourhoods: the keep, the hall, the chapel and the knights' houses inside the walls
armourers and smiths below the south gate
shops and houses down from the gate
potters, vintners and homes at the lower town's foot

outskirts.name: the vines
outskirts.why: vines on the rock's warm east slope

outskirts.name: the lower fields
outskirts.why: barley and beans between the town and the cove

Cinderwick.purpose: the fire country's harbour: fishing boats and the coaster that calls for Hearthold's goods; charcoal kilns and a black-sand glassworks; the quay is the region's way to the sea
Cinderwick.setting: a black-sand cove between the flows, the young flow steaming to the east; the Ash Coast path and the Ember Way meet here
neighbourhoods: fishers' houses and net lofts along the beach
the kilns, the glassworks and the coopers
the stone quay, the chandler and the harbour office

outskirts.name: the kilns
outskirts.why: charcoal from the dead forest; black-sand glass

Lagoon Landing.purpose: the isles' town: boats, fishing and the diving trade off the reef wrecks (Brine), the naturalist's house, net and sail lofts, the boatyard; the ferry to Driftwood and the boats to the other isles leave from here
Lagoon Landing.setting: the neck of the main isle between the ferry pier on the open north shore and the sheltered lagoon (a drowned crater)
neighbourhoods: boathouses and stilt houses on the lagoon
net and sail lofts, the chandler
the ferry pier, the harbour office and the inn

outskirts.name: the boatyard
outskirts.why: hulls on the slip, the repair shed

Highgarth.purpose: slate from its quarries and wool from the summer pastures, sawn timber from the valley's larches; the drovers' inn on the Garth Road; it sends slate, timber and wool down to Cogsworth. Its old trade over the north pass stopped when the Starfall brought the rockfall down; the road beyond waits for a later region
Highgarth.setting: a sheltered valley on the upper Cog inside the range: stepped streets on the east bank, stone houses on retaining walls, steep wooded slopes and snow on the peaks round it
neighbourhoods: the stepped main street: the inn, the smithy, the store
the slate works and the quarrymen's houses up the east slope
houses over the river meadows, the sawmill by the Cog

outskirts.name: the slate quarry
outskirts.why: slate for the roofs of Cogsworth and the valley

outskirts.name: the in-fields
outskirts.why: hay for the winter and oats, walled

outskirts.name: the folds
outskirts.why: sheepfolds below the summer pastures

Neon Harbour: the old waterfront.purpose: the city's first streets, round the ria's head where the Glint falls gave the first crossing: narrow lanes, old houses, small businesses (chandlers, cafes, pawn shops, a ferry office) and the Bridgefoot square
Neon Harbour: the old waterfront.setting: the rock between the Glint's falls and the old quays at the head of the ria
neighbourhoods: the oldest houses between the falls
the first quays, now cafes and small trade

Neon Harbour: the docks.purpose: warehouses, boats, repair yards, workshops and cargo handling: the deep water of the ria's east side, the steamer pier, the fish market, the cranes and the slip
Neon Harbour: the docks.setting: the ria's east shore from the old quays down to its mouth
neighbourhoods: the long quay, the cranes and the bonded warehouses
the repair yard and the boat slip near the mouth

outskirts.name: the slip
outskirts.why: boats hauled out for repair

Neon Harbour: the Lanes and the East Sho.purpose: closely packed homes and flats with courtyards, washing over the lanes, pot plants, corner shops and a school; the East Shore's terraces face the open sea
Neon Harbour: the Lanes and the East Sho.setting: between the old waterfront and the Company district, and along the east coast
neighbourhoods: terraces along the sea front, the lido

Neon Harbour: the Company district.purpose: larger buildings, offices, the Company's tower and the maglev terminus; deliveries and concentrated street activity; the Company crater fenced in its yard to the north, its light sold as neon
Neon Harbour: the Company district.setting: the flats east of the old town, round the terminus
neighbourhoods: the maglev terminus and its square
offices, arcades and the neon boulevard
the fenced crater and its works

outskirts.name: the Company's yard
outskirts.why: the Company crater, fenced; its shard light pumped to the neon

Neon Harbour: the Heights and the Skypor.purpose: terraces, stairs and elevated walks over the city; the funicular up from the canal basin; the Skyport's mooring masts on the crown, where the airships ride above the roofs; views over the ria, the docks and the sea
Neon Harbour: the Heights and the Skypor.setting: the headland west of the ria, over three knolls
neighbourhoods: the Skyport: its masts, the terminal and the hangar
houses on the contours, stairs between
the canal basin and the funicular station

Canalside.purpose: market gardens and the carters' and bargees' houses on the Lull Road where it comes into the city beside the Lull Cut
Canalside.setting: the flat land between the Lull Road and the canal, west of the old town

outskirts.name: the market gardens
outskirts.why: vegetables and flowers for the city's markets

Glintside.purpose: a village of mill houses and laundries along the Glint above the falls, now the city's northern edge, where the maglev comes in
Glintside.setting: the Glint's banks north of the old town

outskirts.name: the allotments
outskirts.why: the city's allotments by the Glint

Halcyon Row.purpose: the launch staff's houses at the cape's neck, named for the Company's station overhead: the canteen, the store, the clinic; a heath buffer of more than 800 px between it and the pad
Halcyon Row.setting: the neck of Launch Cape, behind the dunes

Lullford.purpose: the lowest bridging place of the Lull: the swing bridge, the toll house, bargees' inns and the mill on the island
Lullford.setting: gravel terraces either side of the river

Driftwood.purpose: the valley's landing place: fishers' cottages, the lighthouse keeper's house, the ferry pier
Driftwood.setting: the cove at the Sleepwater's mouth under the Headland

Gullwick.purpose: a fishing cove on the open coast: boats on the beach, net lofts
Gullwick.setting: the cove west of the delta

Cinder Springs.purpose: hot springs where the sea seeps into the warm flank: the bath house and lodgings

the Lode.purpose: the iron and copper mine: the mine house, the smithy, the miners' bunkhouse
the Lode.setting: the massif foothills above Dust Gulch

Ember forge.purpose: the forge at the caldera lip, using the crater's heat: the forge hall, the ore store

Launch Cape.purpose: the Company's launch site: rockets go up over open sea, away from people (W8); the assembly hall, the workshops and the propellant stores in the cape's middle, the pad at its tip; a buffer of open heath between the pad and every house
Launch Cape.setting: the headland past the city, exposed to the sea on three sides
neighbourhoods: the launch pad, its tower and the service apron
the assembly hall, workshops, stores and the control bunker

outskirts.name: the works yard
outskirts.why: carts and the transporter road to the pad

districts: Neon Harbour: the Lanes and the East Shore
Neon Harbour: the Heights and the Skyport

C1.name: the Highgarth pass
C1.open_to: the rockfall (a viewpoint, a sign and the road beyond seen, not walked)
C1.movement: closed: the rockfall and the road beyond are not walkable ground
C1.navigation: closed: no route, path plan or act 1 beat runs past the rockfall; the road beyond is listed under closed_routes, not routes
C1.travel: closed: no waystone, station, shortcut, ferry or fast-travel target beyond it
C1.opens: later, with a region north of the range; the road runs on over the col at the canvas's top edge, so the new region joins there without moving a town or rescaling the continent
C1.separate_from_story: the act 1 crossings are the ridge col (W2) and the Fells saddle, 1.3 km west; the Northway shares no ground with them

label_zoom.continent (the 1920 and 3840 maps): regions, the large and medium towns and the city, the stone circle, the principal routes (roads, rail and ferries) and the closed pass; nothing else
label_zoom.region (the insets): every settlement, gate, crater, peak, biome, water and route in the inset
label_zoom.reference (map55-reference): every name on the continent, at 3x

journeys.journey: Lullford - Canalside - Neon Harbour - Halcyon Row - Launch Cape
